ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, points D and E are located on sides AC and BC respectively, and $AD=DE$, $AB=BE$, $\angle A=70^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle CED$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AD=DE$, and $AB=BE$\\
Also $BD= BD$\\
Therefore, $\triangle ABD \cong \triangle EBD$ (SSS)\\
Thus, $\angle BED = \angle A = 70^\circ$\\
Therefore, $\angle CED = 180^\circ - \angle BED = 180^\circ - 70^\circ = \boxed{110^\circ}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is at the lower left, B is at the lower right, and C is above; point D is located on side AC, and point E is located on side BC; from D, connect respectively to B and E, forming triangle ABD and triangle EBD. In the figure it can be seen that C, E, B are on the same straight line, and A, D, C are on the same straight line. Reasoning: Consider triangles ABD and EBD. The problem statement gives AD=DE, AB=BE; at the same time BD is the common side of the two triangles, so BD=BD. Therefore, triangles ABD and EBD are congruent by SSS, where A corresponds to E. Thus corresponding angles are equal, ∠DEB=∠DAB. Because D is on AC, ray AD is collinear with AC, so ∠DAB=∠CAB=∠A=70°. Also because C, E, B are collinear, rays EC and EB are in opposite directions, so ∠CED and ∠DEB are supplementary angles. Therefore ∠CED=180°−70°=110°.
